title: Availability, Redundancy, and Scaling
summary: Connect workload growth and failure domains to resilient infrastructure choices.
objectives: Identify redundancy and failure-domain concerns across infrastructure layers.

vocab.def: Adding systems or nodes to provide more total capability.
A set of components that may be affected by the same failure.

sections.heading: Growth has choices
sections.body: Scale up adds capability to one system; scale out adds systems or nodes. The right choice depends on workload, latency, cost, operations, availability, and policy.

sections.heading: Redundancy crosses domains
sections.body: Availability may depend on multiple nodes, storage, network paths, power, cooling, and monitoring. A second server does not remove a shared switch, power path, or cooling-zone failure domain.

practice.prompt: Why inspect failure domains when adding a second compute node?
practice.answer: Both nodes may still depend on the same network, storage, power, or cooling component.

quiz.question: What is scale out?
options: Adding memory to one server only

lab.objective: Compare synthetic availability and scaling choices.

futureCompetencyCandidates: analyze AI/cloud availability and failure domains
reflectionPrompt: Which shared dependency could defeat an otherwise redundant design?
